hook_text: Every rand that leaves a business leaves a trail. Here is the notebook that catches all of it.
clip_script: The repair shop pays for spare parts, wages, rent, a new tool, the owner's withdrawal, and the bank quietly takes charges and an insurance debit order. All of it goes in the cash payments journal. One line per payment: EFT number, date, who was paid, how much left the bank. Then the same amount again in its lane: wages, repair parts, or sundry with a name. Drawings? Not an expense, but money out, so it is in. New tool? An asset, but money out, so it is in. At month-end: six thousand plus four thousand two hundred plus fifteen thousand one hundred and twenty-five, twenty-five thousand three hundred and twenty-five rand. Same as the bank column. Balanced.
visual_style: A whiteboard notebook with lanes labelled Doc, Day, Payee, Bank, Wages, Parts and Sundry, papers flying in from an EFT receipt, a supplier slip and a bank statement, and a tick when the totals match.
mood: Brisk and tidy, the satisfaction of a balanced page.
pacing: Fast pile-up of payments, a steady walk through the lanes, two quick traps, and a satisfying total.
